params.question: In the WHO classification of xerophthalmia, which stage marks the critical threshold requiring urgent specialist referral?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: X1A is an early stage where the conjunctiva loses its normal shine. It responds well to vitamin A supplementation at the Primary Health Centre; the cornea is not yet involved.
X1B (Bitot's spots) is still a conjunctival sign — foamy white triangular deposits on the temporal bulbar conjunctiva. The corneas remain clear, and treatment at the PHC level is sufficient.

Once the cornea is involved at stage X2, progression to keratomalacia and irreversible blindness can be rapid. Stages XN through X1B respond to vitamin A at the PHC; X2 and beyond need urgent specialist care.

answers.text: X3A — Keratomalacia involving less than one-third of the cornea

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: X3A represents corneal melting that has already begun. Referral should have occurred at the earlier stage X2 (corneal xerosis), before irreversible corneal destruction started.

overallFeedback.feedback: The cornea is the referral line. Stages XN, X1A, and X1B involve only the retina and conjunctiva and respond to vitamin A at the PHC. Stage X2 (corneal xerosis) signals imminent risk of permanent corneal damage, making specialist referral urgent.
Correct. The cornea is the dividing line: stages XN through X1B are managed at the PHC with vitamin A; stage X2 and beyond require urgent specialist referral.

interactions.label: Why are alkali chemical burns more destructive to the eye than acid burns?

params.question: Why are alkali chemical burns more destructive to the eye than acid burns?

answers.text: Alkali generates a higher temperature at the ocular surface than acid

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The difference is not thermal. Alkali and acid burns differ in the type of tissue necrosis they produce, which determines how deeply the chemical penetrates.

answers.text: Alkali causes coagulative necrosis that extends deeper into the cornea

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Coagulative necrosis is the pattern caused by acid, not alkali. Acid denatures surface proteins into a coagulum that actually limits how deep the acid can penetrate.

answers.text: Alkali causes liquefactive necrosis, dissolving cell membranes and penetrating continuously until removed

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Alkali dissolves cell membranes through liquefactive necrosis. No protein barrier forms to halt penetration, so alkali passes through the cornea into the anterior chamber and continues causing damage minute by minute until irrigation removes it.

answers.text: Alkali selectively destroys limbal stem cells while acid spares them

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Both alkali and acid can damage limbal stem cells in severe burns. The critical difference is the necrosis pattern: alkali causes liquefactive necrosis with no self-limiting barrier, allowing continuous deep penetration.

overallFeedback.feedback: Acid causes coagulative necrosis: it denatures surface proteins into a barrier that limits penetration depth. Alkali causes liquefactive necrosis: it dissolves cell membranes without forming any barrier, penetrating through the cornea into the anterior chamber until physically removed by irrigation. This is why irrigation must come first — before history, examination, or ophthalmology referral.
Correct. Liquefactive necrosis allows alkali to penetrate continuously — that is precisely why copious irrigation before anything else is the single most important first action in a chemical burn.

interactions.label: A 55-year-old diabetic presents with a blind, painful right eye. B-scan ultrason

params.question: A 55-year-old diabetic presents with a blind, painful right eye. B-scan ultrasonography reveals no intraocular mass. Which procedure is most appropriate?

answers.text: Enucleation — the entire globe must be removed to prevent sympathetic ophthalmia

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Enucleation is mandatory when a tumour is present or suspected, because scleral emissary canals allow tumour escape. Here, B-scan has excluded a mass and there is no history of penetrating injury. Sympathetic ophthalmia risk arises from penetrating trauma, not from a blind painful eye per se.

answers.text: Exenteration — all orbital contents should be cleared given the diabetes

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Exenteration removes the entire orbital contents and is reserved for malignancies with extraocular spread or rhino-orbital mucormycosis. Diabetes alone does not indicate exenteration; a blind painful eye without orbital invasion or tumour calls for evisceration.

answers.text: Evisceration — intraocular contents are removed, preserving the scleral shell

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: With no tumour on B-scan, evisceration is appropriate. It removes intraocular contents while preserving the sclera, extraocular muscles, and orbital anatomy — giving excellent socket motility and cosmetic outcome.

answers.text: Conservative management with cyclopllegics and systemic analgesics

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A blind, painful eye unresponsive to medical therapy causes ongoing suffering and carries risks of phthisis bulbi. Definitive surgical relief through evisceration is indicated when B-scan has excluded an intraocular mass.

overallFeedback.feedback: Apply the decision algorithm: (1) Is a tumour present or suspected? → Enucleate (scleral emissary canals allow tumour escape). (2) Blind painful eye, no tumour on B-scan? → Eviscerate (preserves scleral shell, better cosmesis). (3) Orbital spread of malignancy or mucormycosis? → Exenterate. Always B-scan before evisceration to rule out a hidden intraocular mass.

Correct. The decision algorithm: tumour present or suspected → enucleate; blind painful eye, no tumour (confirmed by B-scan) → eviscerate; disease with orbital spread → exenterate. The B-scan is never optional before evisceration.

interactions.label: The National Programme for Control of Blindness was renamed in 2017 to include '

params.question: The National Programme for Control of Blindness was renamed in 2017 to include 'Visual Impairment'. What does this expanded name reflect?

answers.text: A shift from community-based outreach to hospital-centred surgical care

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The programme continues to deliver community-based services — rural outreach camps, school eye screening, and vitamin A supplementation. The name change broadens the conditions addressed, not the delivery model.

answers.text: Expansion of the programme's mandate from blindness alone to all degrees of visual impairment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The 2017 renaming acknowledges that visual impairment short of total blindness — mild, moderate, and severe — also impairs daily function and economic productivity. The expanded mandate ensures these conditions are captured during field surveys and receive programmatic attention.

answers.text: Transfer of programme coordination from the central government to state health departments

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The programme remains a centrally sponsored national initiative. The name change reflects a broader clinical mandate — covering all levels of visual impairment — not an administrative restructuring.

answers.text: Replacement of Vision 2020 targets with newer WHO sustainable development goals

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Vision 2020 (co-founded by WHO and the IAPB) and the NPCBVI are complementary initiatives. India joined Vision 2020 as a founding partner. The NPCBVI's 2017 renaming broadened its mandate to cover all visual impairment, not just blindness.

overallFeedback.feedback: The addition of 'Visual Impairment' broadens the programme from addressing only blindness (acuity below 3/60 WHO, or 6/60 by Indian field criteria) to covering all grades of visual impairment — mild, moderate, and severe. The programme's delivery model — free cataract surgery, school screening, vitamin A supplementation, and rural outreach camps — continues as before.

Correct. The expanded name captures the full spectrum — from mild impairment (6/12 to 6/18) through moderate and severe impairment to blindness — aligning India's programme with the global recognition that treatable visual loss at any level deserves intervention.
